title: Generate a brand logo
summary: Use an image model to develop a logo, then refine its colors, icon and wordmark, small-size detail, and black-and-white versions.
outcomes: A recommended or selected logo direction that fits the company and its first real uses.
Coherent icon and wordmark arrangements, suitable color and monochrome versions, and a mark that remains recognizable at the sizes needed.
Usable artwork with a short explanation of its design choices and any unresolved limitations.
guidance:
Start with a capable image model and a clear design brief. The useful work is choosing a direction and refining the colors, icon and wordmark, simplicity, and behavior across real uses. Keep existing assets and decisions in use where possible.

Reuse the company name, audience, offer, tone, existing artwork, colors, rejected directions, and intended uses from context. Infer a sensible starting direction when you can. Ask only when a missing preference materially changes the work. A new logo does not require a complete brand strategy or UI color system.

Develop the brief, compare the actual artwork, and make focused improvements. A useful recommendation explains the design choices and tradeoffs. Preserve an existing selection; keep a proposed direction distinct from a final choice.

notes.text: UM’s default recommendation for an early startup logo is to use a capable image model and spend effort on art direction and iteration. A separate design service is useful when the work needs specialist judgment or production requirements that the available agent methods cannot meet.

metadata.supportReason: Image-generation APIs produce the candidates; the founder picks the primary logo.
